_comment: Runtime feature-gate overrides, read by src/services/analytics/growthbook.ts via CLAUDE_FEATURE_FLAGS_FILE (set in serge.env). Highest priority: this file > _openBuildDefaults > the call site's default. RUNTIME gates only (tengu_* names read through getFeatureValue_*) — it has no power over build-time feature() macros, which scripts/build.ts resolves to literals before bundling. Unknown keys are ignored, so a stale entry is inert rather than harmful. Takes effect on the next serge start; no rebuild.
_why_tengu_herring_clock: TEAM MEMORY, off since 2026-08-14. isTeamMemoryEnabled() (memdir/teamMemPaths.ts:73) is isAutoMemoryEnabled() AND this gate, whose call-site default is TRUE and which is absent from _openBuildDefaults — so team memory was on by default. On a single-user machine there is no team, and the cost was real: loadMemoryPrompt() took the buildCombinedMemoryPrompt branch, which spends prompt on a private-vs-team scope decision for every memory type, and the engine split saves across two directories — 60 fact files had accumulated under projects/*/memory/team/ across 8 projects, which nothing surfaced at session start. Measured with the live binary via --dump-system-prompt: 27,700 B / 232 lines with team scope, 25,844 B / 221 lines without — 1,856 B (~465 tokens) off EVERY request, and no free seat in this roster offers prompt caching. Nothing is stranded: memory-load.sh now surfaces the existing team store alongside the private one, and new saves land in a single project store instead of scattering. To revert: set true (or delete the key) and restart.
